name: High blood pressure (hypertension)
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> High blood pressure (hypertension). Check question: Has a doctor or nurse ever told you that your BP is high or borderline? Yes, high / Yes, borderline (lifestyle-only mode) / No / Not sure (suggest a BP check). Follow-ups: Do you take any medicine for BP? No / Yes / Not sure; if Yes: water pill (diuretic) / a medicine ending in -pril or -sartan / spironolactone, eplerenone or amiloride / other / I don't know; Has a doctor told you that you have kidney disease? Yes / No / Not sure; Are you pregnant or planning a pregnancy?; optional home BP log and lab values (eGFR, potassium, lipids, HbA1c)

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose high blood pressure; repeated readings reviewed by a doctor are needed.
The app never suggests starting, stopping, skipping or changing a BP medicine or dose, and food changes do not replace prescribed medicines.
Emergency: a reading of 180/120 mmHg or more with chest pain, breathlessness, back pain, numbness or weakness, vision changes, trouble speaking, severe headache or confusion. Seek emergency care now.
Pregnancy: BP 160/110 or more, severe headache, vision changes, upper abdominal pain, sudden swelling of face or hands, breathlessness or reduced baby movements need urgent care.

Potassium-enriched low-sodium salt substitutes and high-potassium advice are not for people with kidney disease, pregnant women, or anyone on ACE inhibitors, ARBs or potassium-sparing diuretics unless their doctor agrees.
Rock salt (sendha namak), black salt and Eno all contain sodium and count toward the daily salt limit.
Anyone on a diuretic (water pill), or with heart, kidney or liver disease, or pregnant: follow your doctor's advice on fluids and salt.
Guidelines differ: Indian, European and WHO guidelines use 140/90 (home 135/85) to diagnose hypertension; ACC/AHA uses 130/80. Your doctor sets your personal target.
requires_doctor_input is true because many users take BP medicines that change potassium and fluid safety; the app sets only general sodium, sugar, fat, alcohol and activity guidance on its own.
